Reason: Did not know it could do that
What it looks like: Photo framing assist, person recognition, Spanish commands, outfit feedback, the touchpad, general AI questions.

Reason: Never thought to try it
What it looks like: Makeup, outfit checks, clothes shopping, follow-up questions.

Reason: Hesitancy and AI shyness
What it looks like: Intimidated by conversational AI. Two dislike new technology in general.

Reason: Forgets to wear or carry it
What it looks like: Constantly wishes she had them when out. Leaves them at home.

Reason: Frames do not stay on the face
What it looks like: Too wide, heavy, slide to the nose. Directly named as a reason for lower use.

Reason: Battery anxiety
What it looks like: Leaves them behind, or carries a backup pair, because the charge may not last.

Reason: A human helper already does it
What it looks like: Appliances, makeup, clothes shopping, photo verification.

Reason: Existing tactile or memory system works
What it looks like: Braille and tactile labels, fixed order, known layout, tabbed appliances, residual vision.

Reason: Mobility limits collapse the use context
What it looks like: Wheelchair and fall risk after a shoulder replacement. Use narrowed to one desk.

Reason: No perceived need in that context
What it looks like: Rural setting with nothing to read, familiar routes, known house, no TV.

Reason: Reliability makes it not worth starting
What it looks like: Cold-start ritual, repeated wake words, drops mid-task.

Reason: Social setting makes it awkward
What it looks like: Church, restaurants, meetings. Voice commands draw attention or interrupt.

Reason: Prescription or lens conflict
What it looks like: Second pair of reading glasses stops it working. Tint darkens residual vision.

Reason: Privacy self-restriction
What it looks like: Bank statements, benefit letters, client records, private photos deliberately kept away from it.

Reason: Patience runs out before the read succeeds
What it looks like: Turns the item over and over, then reaches for another app. Named six times unprompted.

Reason: One bad answer retires the task
What it looks like: A single fabrication ends that use case. Return needs outside proof, not a retry.

Reason: Never tried, expects failure
What it looks like: Long documents, appliance panels, live mode. Ruled out in advance, no failure on record.

Reason: Existing habit wins
What it looks like: Asks the smart speaker or the search engine out of years of practice. The glasses never get the question.

Reason: Prepares ahead so it is not needed
What it looks like: Studies the menu at home. Asks a friend to meet at the door. Avoids dark venues.

Reason: Nervous about calling a human volunteer
What it looks like: Does not know who will answer. Does not want to spend a stranger's time. Paid agents feel safer.

Reason: Barred on safety grounds
What it looks like: Stated as doctrine. Never a mobility tool, whatever it describes.

Reason: Output cannot beat the room
What it looks like: Restaurants, street noise, church. Cannot hear the answer, so the task is dropped.

Reason: Vendor distrust
What it looks like: Declines live conversation because of ad targeting. Same data, different company, different comfort.

Reason: Loss and breakage risk
What it looks like: A $250 pair with no impact rating. Left at home for running, transit and crowds. One report of a blind walker breaking a pair on a wall.

Reason: Battery degradation and a sealed cell
What it looks like: Runtime falls year on year, the cell cannot be replaced, and use falls with it.

Reason: Pressure on the face across a day
What it looks like: Not session discomfort. Named alongside battery as the reason a heavy user became occasional.

Reason: Distrust learned from someone else
What it looks like: Currency reading retired on the strength of a failure watched in another user's video. Never personally attempted.

Reason: The people around the user refuse enrollment
What it looks like: Wife and daughter declined to be added, so the household's most valuable feature was never tested.

Reason: Parents or partner already do it
What it looks like: Mail, groceries, menus, labels. Where a person is on hand the device is never reached for.

Reason: Will not point the camera in a private space
What it looks like: Bathrooms and changing rooms. The wearer self-restricts to protect bystanders.

Reason: Routes visual work to a human instead
What it looks like: Rates the AI 2 of 5 and calls a volunteer for anything that matters. The AI is the fallback, not the default.

Reason: Never tried the continuous mode
What it looks like: Two years of daily use, unsure whether the feature exists on his own device.

Reason: No context for the task
What it looks like: Describes himself as a homebody. Person recognition, social settings and navigation have no occasion to arise.

Reason: Does not know it is a general AI
What it looks like: Nine months of daily use as a one-step reader. Never asked a follow-up question. Learned during the interview that the assistant is general purpose.

Reason: Satisfied enough to stop asking
What it looks like: Happy with mail and ingredients, so never investigates what else it does. Says five times that she is not asking enough.

Reason: Outside the peer channel
What it looks like: Left the forums years ago. One friend is the whole information source. Public tutorials are made by and for sighted users.

Reason: Read as suspicious in a shop
What it looks like: Task use confined to one store where staff know her. Announces the device pre-emptively anywhere else.

Reason: Bystanders treat her as sighted
What it looks like: Named as the largest barrier to outdoor use. People stop making way and start gesturing once the glasses are on.

Reason: Disconnects when she moves
What it looks like: Bending or looking down stops the session. Switched back to earbuds for a cleaning job.

Reason: The live voice is unpleasant
What it looks like: Echoing and tunnel-like, and it masks natural hearing. Tried a handful of times and abandoned.

Reason: Believed the feature was unavailable here
What it looks like: Never tried person recognition because he understood it was not offered in the United States.

Reason: Crowds consume the attention
What it looks like: Penn Station takes all the cognitive load he has, so the features go unused exactly where they would help most.

Reason: Never set up the volunteer service
What it looks like: Uses Be My Eyes on the phone and has never connected it to the glasses in fifteen months.

Reason: Does not know the wording
What it looks like: Calls the trigger phrase the magic words and cannot reliably produce it. Blames himself.

Reason: Judged the tool before needing it
What it looks like: Thought people using text to speech were lazy. Says that belief is still slowing his own adoption down.

Reason: Will not ask the question she fears
What it looks like: Asks for a general description rather than name the snake she is afraid of. Wants to know and does not want to know.

Reason: Keeps it away from the pharmacy label
What it looks like: Comfortable with the dosage instructions read aloud, unwilling to have her name on the bottle captured.

Reason: Never thought to try it
What it looks like: Framing feedback before a photo, describing a laptop screen, outfit feedback, what the buttons do.

Reason: Satisfied with what it already does
What it looks like: Never asks a follow-up because the first description is enough. Satisfaction reads as sufficiency and caps the request list.

Reason: An established tactile system already works
What it looks like: Appliances tabbed, spices labelled by touch and kept in a fixed order. The task was solved before the device arrived.

Reason: Would not touch the phone settings
What it looks like: Declined to switch Wi-Fi networks in a restaurant for fear of not getting the connection back.

Reason: Doing without was the baseline
What it looks like: Left a graduate degree because the reading could not be done. The task never became a task performed badly.

Reason: Cannot get to where it would help
What it looks like: No public transport she can reach, because the crossings between her and the pickup point were never learned.
